clue.text: Military type who sounds a bit of a nut

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for a bit of a nut is said out loud, not written

parts.note: the kernel is the edible inner part of a nut

explanation.surface: An eccentric army officer is described as being slightly crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' suggests madness, but here it is the food: the kernel, which said aloud matches the officer's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer, so a military type.

clue.text: A hundred wave a game man

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a ripple is a small wave

explanation.surface: A crowd of a hundred people waves to a sporting man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' here means lame, an old word for a damaged leg, not sporting.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive word for a person lame in the leg, which is what 'game' meant.

clue.text: Falling for the finesse of a would-be partner?

definitions.text: the finesse of a would-be partner?

explanation.surface: Falling in love with the clever play of a bridge partner.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a finesse is a play that may lose a trick, here in the hearts suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling in love with someone, and at bridge a failed finesse that gives up a card in the red suit of hearts.

clue.text: Apparently the navy is lacking an ancient Orkney language

parts.note: if something is lacking there is no such thing
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The navy apparently lacks speakers of an old Orkney tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' tells you to read 'the navy is lacking' as 'no RN'. Norn was the Norse language of Orkney and Shetland, extinct by the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scandinavian tongue was once spoken in the Orkney and Shetland islands of Scotland.

clue.text: Descent by rope over a period

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the rope word above the period word

parts.note: a rope is a line
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A climber descends by rope over a length of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' suggests abseiling, but it is family ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, a family's line of descent.

clue.text: Footwear for one who misses his footing

explanation.surface: A shoe suited to someone who keeps stumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipper is a soft indoor shoe, and literally a person who slips, losing their footing.

clue.text: Appearing to view the Chinese porcelain exhibition

parts.note: to view is to see
Ming porcelain, from the Ming dynasty, would be the subject of such an exhibition

explanation.surface: Someone shows up to look round a show of Chinese porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: Ming is the Chinese dynasty famous for its porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeming means appearing to be so, giving an outward impression.

clue.text: Confession of a trickster venerated in Russia

explanation.surface: A con man confesses in front of a holy image.
explanation.walkthrough: A trickster confessing says 'I con'; in Russian Orthodoxy, painted images of saints are venerated.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickster's admission that he cons, and a sacred painted image venerated in the Orthodox Church of Russia.

clue.text: Simplest of chapels for the first Christians

explanation.surface: The plainest chapels belong to the earliest believers.
explanation.definitionFit: The most basic, rudimentary place of worship, and the early Christian community of the apostles' era.

clue.text: Sovereigns is what the author asks from his publisher

definitions.text: what the author asks from his publisher

explanation.surface: Gold coins are what a writer wants from the publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereigns' looks like gold coins, a natural payment, but means kings and queens.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings and queens collectively, and the percentage of sales paid to a writer.

clue.text: I can copy rules in order to obtain protection against contingencies

indicators.note: to order letters is to arrange them afresh, so these words are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone copies regulations in order to gain cover against mishaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order to' reads as a single phrase, but 'in' belongs to the fodder and 'order' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract with an underwriter pays out if a stated mishap occurs, guarding against contingencies.

clue.text: A horse for £25

explanation.surface: Someone is selling a horse for twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'pony' is twenty-five pounds sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A small breed of horse, and British money slang for the sum of twenty-five pounds.

clue.text: Herb Spence of Coventry fame

explanation.surface: A man named Herb Spence is famous in Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Basil Spence was the architect of the new Coventry Cathedral, built after the Second World War; 'Herb' poses as a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant culinary leaf, and the first name of the architect Sir Basil Spence, who designed Coventry Cathedral.

clue.text: Penny sick? Then maybe she should take one

definitions.text: Then maybe she should take one

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: If Penny is feeling unwell, perhaps she should take some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but gives P, the abbreviation for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone feeling unwell might swallow a tablet of medicine.

clue.text: Airy? More likely to be scared

explanation.surface: An airy person is more easily frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy' is British slang for nervous or scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Breezy and full of air, and in British slang nervous, easily frightened.

clue.text: Frightening description of a hirsute beast

explanation.surface: A shaggy animal is a scary sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for alarming or dangerous, and literally covered in fur, as a shaggy animal is.

clue.text: Sore back I have is wearing

indicators.note: back tells us the word for sore is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a sore back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the body part, but it is the reversal signal on 'Sore', giving EROS, followed by IVE from 'I have'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing in the sense of gradually abrading or wearing away, as water does to rock.

clue.text: Down-to earth seriousness

explanation.surface: Practical, level-headed solemnity.
explanation.definitionFit: The force pulling things down to earth, and solemn seriousness of manner.

clue.text: Gorge cheese

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat lots of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England, and the village gave its name to the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous ravine in Somerset, and the hard English cheese named after that village.

clue.text: Opportunity supported by Liberal section of the church

indicators.note: in a down answer, supported by means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance

explanation.surface: Liberal backing gives the church faction its opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Armada breaks up northern and eastern festival

indicators.note: an armada that breaks up is scattered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A great fleet breaks up as sailors head north and east to a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks up' shuffles ARMADA into RAMADA, followed by N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim holy month of fasting, observed widely in the Middle East and Asia.

clue.text: The sort of account one expects to run between two banks

definitions.text: one expects to run between two banks

explanation.surface: A kind of bank account that runs between two banks.
explanation.walkthrough: A current account is an everyday bank account; a river's flow runs between its two banks.
explanation.definitionFit: An everyday bank account for payments, and the flow of water running between a river's banks.

clue.text: In restaurants an artist may take wine from them

indicators.note: In signals that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: cafes are small restaurants
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter dining out may help himself to some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass jugs are what restaurant drinkers pour their wine from.

clue.text: Bound to display pronounced trust

indicators.note: pronounced signals that we hear the word trust spoken

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to show marked faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up tightly with rope, as a bird is before roasting.

clue.text: Bill and he suffer pain

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bill and another man are both in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but means an account, abbreviated AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to hurt continuously, to feel pain.

clue.text: Butters up maiden-that is what it does

definitions.text: Butters up maiden-that is what it does

parts.words: Butters up maiden-that is what it does
parts.note: the clue describes oily, ingratiating flattery as the thing that butters up a young woman

explanation.surface: Someone flatters a young woman, and that is the purpose of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous flattery is what is used to sweet-talk or ingratiate oneself with someone.

clue.text: Cream bun for onetime Chinese premier

explanation.surface: A cream bun is named after a former Chinese prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Chou En-lai (Zhou Enlai) was China's first premier; a choux bun is a cream-filled pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry bun filled with cream, and Chou En-lai, premier of China from 1949 to 1976.

clue.text: The cut in foreign currency dealings

definitions.text: The cut in foreign currency dealings

parts.words: The cut in foreign currency dealings
parts.note: the clue describes the fee or premium a dealer charges when exchanging one currency for another

explanation.definitionFit: A premium or commission charged when changing money or exchanging currencies.

clue.text: Georgia double crazy

indicators.note: double means the abbreviation for Georgia is written out twice

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Georgia goes doubly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for senile or foolishly infatuated, i.e. mad.

clue.text: Diplomat indicted with clandestine amatory liaisons

parts.note: indicted means formally charged
secret romances are affairs, here in the French spelling affaires

explanation.surface: A diplomat is indicted over secret love affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The second word uses the French spelling of 'affairs', as the diplomatic title is French.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a diplomat who deputises for an ambassador or heads a minor mission.

clue.text: Failed to deflate

explanation.surface: Someone failed to let the air out.
explanation.definitionFit: To let somebody down is to fail or disappoint them; to let a tyre down is to deflate it.

clue.text: Injured domestic animal put in the outhouse

indicators.note: put in signals that one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an outhouse is a shed
a cat is a domestic animal

explanation.surface: An injured pet has been placed in the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathed means harmed or hurt, the rarely seen opposite of unscathed.
